Handwritten-text-recognition (HTR) models are routine infrastructure in the digital humanities, yet
they are handled as black boxes: a file and a character error rate. This project asks what can be
read from their weights, and whether a language model acting as a programmer can change those
weights in code, **without gradient descent**, so that the model reads better.

The method follows R. Takehi, J. Teoh, A. Zhang and O. Khattab,
["Sparks of Weight-Space Programming"](https://rikiyat.github.io/blog/weight-space-programming/)
(2 November 2026). Here it is applied to a family of kraken line recognisers fine-tuned on historical
German handwriting, to a LoRA adapter of a vision-language model, and to a family of TrOCR models.
The programmers were Claude models (Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1). Each worked in a
sandbox with a fixed budget of measurements and a fixed rule for keeping an edit.

::: {.project-facts}
**Finding so far.** No weight edit has yet done better than a cheap alternative. The one budgeted
session with a held-out gain whose interval excludes 0 matches a short retrain on corrected data and
does not beat it. Reading the weights, on the other hand, turned up defects in the project's own data.
:::

## How the work is done

Every session follows a research protocol that was written before the sessions it governs:

1. **Preregister.** Hypotheses, with predicted direction and size, are written down before the first
   measurement of a session.
2. **Held-out once.** The held-out set is out of the programmer's reach and is scored once, after the
   edit is frozen.
3. **Intervals, not point estimates.** Every difference carries a page-clustered 95 % interval; a gain
   whose interval contains 0 is not a gain.
4. **Report everything.** Refused edits, failed sessions and data defects are results.
5. **Compare with the cheap alternatives.** An edit is only interesting if it beats averaging,
   interpolation and a short retrain.

## What is here

- **[Research protocol](protocol/index.md):** the rules, every amendment with its date and reason, and
  the current status.
- **[Journal](protocol/journal/index.md):** dated entries in the order the work happened. Entries are
  not rewritten; corrections are new entries.
- **[Results](protocol/results.md):** the numbers, each traceable to a run, a data-set hash and the
  model digests.
- **[Activation atlas](atlas.qmd):** an interactive explorer of what two kraken models compute along a
  line, with the controls and the two failed gates that limit what it may claim.
- **[Repository](https://github.com/thodel/weightspace):** code, run records, reports and figures.
  Model weights are not in the repository; of the line images, only the twelve practice lines shown in
  the atlas are.
